stocks.discussion_driver: CarMax surged ~5% on September 29 after posting a blowout Q2 FY2027 beat: EPS $1.16 vs. $0.73 estimate (+59% upside), revenue $7.88B vs. $7.06B expected, and retail/wholesale unit sales up 14.7% YoY. The company also announced plans to resume share buybacks in Q4 FY2026, signaling management confidence despite the bearish macro backdrop.
bull_case: 59% EPS beat and 14.7% YoY unit sales growth signals a major recovery in the used-car market; planned buyback resumption in Q4 FY2026 demonstrates balance-sheet strength
CarMax is up ~57% YTD as improving consumer auto-buying trends and better financing spreads boost profitability across retail and wholesale channels
bear_case: Analyst consensus price target of ~$57 sits below the post-earnings price of $59.23, with a Hold consensus suggesting limited near-term upside from current levels
Trailing P/E of 36x looks stretched for a cyclical auto retailer; elevated consumer credit stress and high interest rates could pressure used-car demand and financing profitability going forward

stocks.discussion_driver: TD Cowen initiated SpaceX (SPCX) with a Buy rating and $200 price target on September 29, citing AI compute leasing as the company's next transformative revenue driver with projections reaching $133B by 2028. The initiation coincided with Starship's successful orbital mission deploying 26 Starlink satellites and performing a controlled landing burn in the Pacific Ocean.
bull_case: TD Cowen projects AI compute leasing revenues scaling from ~$14B in 2026 to $133B by 2028, potentially making SpaceX a dominant cloud and AI infrastructure player alongside hyperscalers

Starlink subscriber growth and Starship's increasing cadence targeting ~1,000 launches per year create a compounding moat in satellite internet and commercial launch services with no direct competitor
bear_case: Stock trades at ~94x sales with no P/E (pre-GAAP-profit), making valuation highly speculative and vulnerable to risk-off sentiment or any execution stumble in the Starship program
IPO lockup expiry in August 2026 triggered a 53% collapse from the $225.64 peak to $104.83 — further insider selling pressure and secondary offerings remain a structural overhang

stocks.discussion_driver: Deutsche Bank upgraded Netflix to Buy from Hold with a $95 price target on September 29, arguing the stock's 22% YTD decline and 40% 12-month underperformance since the Warner Bros. Discovery merger collapse creates a compelling re-entry point. The bank views current valuation as unjustifiably depressed given Netflix's double-digit revenue growth trajectory.
bull_case: Deutsche Bank upgrade highlights that NFLX at ~$71 with a forward P/E of 21x represents significant value; analyst consensus target of $93.66 implies over 31% upside as WBD deal overhang fades
Advertising-supported tier and planned FIFA World Cup 2026 live content could drive a major re-acceleration in subscriber growth and average revenue per user through the back half of 2026
bear_case: Stock down 40.6% over 12 months and has underperformed the S&P 500 by ~57 percentage points; RSI at 38.9 points to ongoing selling pressure with no clear near-term catalyst beyond the upgrade
Competition from Disney+, Amazon Prime Video, and Max continues to fragment streaming market share; content spending inflation and currency headwinds pressure free cash flow margins

stocks.discussion_driver: Argus downgraded Warner Bros. Discovery to Sell on September 29 citing that the Paramount Skydance acquisition at $31/share is now imminent following antitrust clearance. With WBD trading at $30.90 — just $0.02 below its 52-week high and $0.10 below the deal price — Argus sees virtually no remaining upside while downside risk is material if the deal encounters any last-minute complications.
bull_case: Potential Paramount Skydance deal close at $31/share offers a near-certain, low-risk return from the current $30.90 level with regulatory clearance already secured
WBD stock has surged ~54% over the past 12 months, and a finalized deal at or near the $31 offer price would represent full realization of that upside for shareholders
bear_case: Stock is essentially at its 52-week high and acquisition price — there is virtually no additional upside, and any deal disruption, renegotiation, or delay would send shares sharply lower
Argus projects a GAAP loss of $0.90/share in 2026 with only a $0.07 recovery in 2027; underlying business fundamentals are weak with negative earnings and declining linear TV revenue

stocks.discussion_driver: J.P. Morgan downgraded PepsiCo from Overweight to Neutral on September 29, cutting its price target 19% to $138 due to persistent weakness in Frito-Lay's North American salty snacks division. Despite some international FIFA World Cup 2026 tailwinds, U.S. snack volumes continue to disappoint as cost-conscious consumers trade down to private-label alternatives, and the stock has now shed 25% from its 52-week high.
bull_case: PEP at a P/E of 17x — near a multi-year valuation low — offers a historically cheap entry point for a mega-cap consumer staples franchise; consensus analyst target of $155 implies over 20% upside
International business showing resilience with FIFA World Cup 2026 driving Pepsi brand engagement globally; the RSI of 51.4 is neutral and the stock is not technically oversold
bear_case: J.P. Morgan's 19% price-target cut to $138 follows a wave of downgrades, signaling fundamental deterioration in Frito-Lay North America — the company's core profit engine — with no clear near-term recovery path

Consumer trade-down to private-label snacks is a structural, not cyclical shift; PEP is down 25% from its 52-week high of $171.48 and consumer confidence at a 12-year low (81.9) could pressure volumes further
